title: strict decrease for the complementary idempotent fibre
statement: Let R→S be a finite-type map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], let R→R₁ be any algebra, p⊂R and P⊂R₁ primes with P over p and bijective canonical residue-field map κ(p)→κ(P) [def-weil-residue-field]. Put C=R₁⊗_R S. Let e∈C be idempotent. Suppose q⊂S is a prime over p at which S/R is quasi-finite, and r⊂C is a prime over P contracting to q with e∉r. Then the number of points with open singleton in Spec(κ(P)⊗_{R₁}(C/(e))) is strictly less than the number in Spec(κ(p)⊗_R S) [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The comparison does not require R→R₁ étale or C[e⁻¹] finite.

proof.text: The bijective canonical residue-field map κ(p)→κ(P) is a field isomorphism. Associativity/cancellation of tensor products identifies κ(P)⊗[R₁](R₁⊗[R]S) with κ(p)⊗[R]S. The corresponding spectrum homeomorphism is compatible with contraction to S. This is the affine ring form of the base-change fibre description and the fibre-prime correspondence.

The fibre of D=C/(e) is the quotient of the fibre of C by the image of e (Mathlib Algebra.TensorProduct.tensorQuotientEquiv). Since e is idempotent, its zero locus is clopen, the complement of D(e). Its spectrum is that clopen subspace, by the quotient/localization identification and the localization basic-open homeomorphism. Isolated points in this open subspace remain isolated in the ambient fibre.

The fibre point corresponding to r is outside the clopen quotient factor because e∉r. Under the residue-field comparison it corresponds to q by hrq. It is isolated because q is quasi-finite, using the quasi-finite/fibre-singleton criterion recorded with the one-prime theorem.

The isolated-point set in the original finite-type field fibre is finite. The clopen inclusion followed by the spectrum homeomorphism gives an injective map from the quotient isolated-point set into it, missing the isolated point corresponding to q. The image is a strict subset; Set.ncard_image_of_injective and Set.ncard_lt_ncard give the strict inequality, also showing the quotient set is finite.
